bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Summary callouts on the "Disciplined Capital Allocation" slide: "71% Avg. OCF/EBITDA", "₹1,200 Cr+ Capex + M&A", "23.0% Post Tax ROCE" and "₹438 Cr Cumulative Dividend" (FY22-FY26 charts).
- Post-tax RoCE series across FY22-FY26 reads 23.4%, 24.4%, 25.4%, 25.2%, 16.6% — i.e. the deck shows FY26 stepping down sharply versus the 23.0% average it headlines.
- Dividend per share across FY22-FY26 reads ₹2.53, ₹4.75, ₹5.75, ₹9.5* and ₹5.25, with the footnote "*Includes ₹3 special dividend"; EPS over the same bars reads ₹15.07, ₹19.31, ₹22.22, ₹22.79, ₹18.45.
- Capex/reinvestment bars for FY22-FY26 read 219, 208, 99, 129, 352 (₹ Cr) — note the last bar is 352 while the FY27 outlook slide cites "₹351 Cr in FY26".
- Operating cash flow bars for FY22-FY26 read 257, 407, 440, 482, 390 (₹ Cr) against OCF/EBITDA of 64%, 75%, 73%, 76%, 66%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Pan-India physical network built over two decades, reaching 97% of India's geography including the semi-urban and rural towns where consumption growth is occurring
- End-to-end integrated model — cash forecasting and replenishment, hardware supply, installation, maintenance, network software and remote monitoring from a single accountable partner, which the SBI mandate is described as validating
- Full-stack ownership in Vision AI — hardware, software and AI models — described as difficult for competitors to replicate; Securens added 10 years of AI-trained data and took the combined entity to roughly double the scale of the nearest competitor
- Category leadership: largest Vision AI platform in India with over 50,000 monitored sites and 36% share; ALGO MVS at approximately 40% market share powering 65,000 machines including the entire SBI network
- Scale and balance sheet — zero-net-debt maintained through FY26 with OCF-to-EBITDA conversion averaging 70%+ over several years, positioning CMS as a beneficiary of industry consolidation as weaker cash-logistics players exit
- Contract quality shift — bidding only for fixed-price service contracts rather than transaction-volume-linked ones, improving certainty of future earnings
- Variable-cost delivery model — ML-driven route optimisation (10%+ routes cut) and a gig workforce covering over 20% of retail cash locations, enabling economical expansion into smaller towns
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Consumption and formalisation slowdown feeding operating deleverage on a largely fixed-cost network — Retail Solutions is exposed to slowdowns in organised consumption and India's retail formalisation. H1 FY26 demonstrated the mechanism: weak consumption suppressed cash collection volumes and created deleverage on a largely fixed-cost network. Mitigants cited are customer and geographic diversification (165 direct-to-retail logos), gig conversion of fixed to variable labour cost, and the rationalisation of low-yield accounts carried out in FY26.
- Digital substitution of cash — The Company's base case is that cash and digital payments are complementary rather than substitutive in India for the foreseeable future, and it tracks transaction velocity, ATM usage patterns and RBI currency-in-circulation data monthly. Management states monthly currency dispensed through ATMs is steady at around Rs 2.5 lakh Cr and rural withdrawals are rising, and that it is accelerating the mix toward Technology & Payment Solutions and Retail in any case. A structural break in this assumption would strike the core revenue engine.
- Fuel, wage inflation and currency movement as live operating cost pressures — Named in the Chairman's 'Risks We Are Watching' as live operating pressures that geopolitical volatility in the Middle East could compound. The stated response is structural rather than eliminating: a variable-cost model through gig delivery, AI-led route optimisation across 4,000+ routes, and fixed-fee managed services contracts that insulate revenue from transaction-volume swings — measures said to reduce the amplitude of the risk, not remove it.
- Commoditisation of Vision AI — Flagged by the Chairman as one of two other actively managed risks. The stated moat against it is the Company's proprietary incident dataset — a defence that erodes if competitors accumulate comparable training data or if the technology itself becomes undifferentiated.
- Competitive intensity in cash logistics and managed services — Flagged by the Chairman as the second actively managed risk, against which the Company claims a proven cyclical playbook. The FY26 experience showed how sharply competitive disruption transmits: a large listed competitor's exit shrank the outsourced ATM base and delayed payments across the ecosystem even as it ultimately handed share to integrated players.
- Cyber security and data privacy — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: threats and vulnerabilities can compromise the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data and information systems. Mitigation is strict adherence to the Information Security policy plus 27 related policies, ISO 27001:2022 ISMS certification, CERT-IN certification for the Remote Monitoring System, and PCI DSS affiliation. The exposure is structural given the Company handles bank cash, card personalisation and surveillance feeds.
- Occupational health and safety across a large field workforce — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Mitigation is internal audits of health and safety practices and working conditions, periodic fire-safety, mock-drill and earthquake-preparedness training, and implementation of an HSE Policy and Fire Safety Policy. The risk is inherent to a business whose delivery is physical cash movement across the country.
- Supply chain resilience — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications, since the nature of the business requires a resilient supply chain for continuous functionality. Mitigation is adherence to the Suppliers' Code of Conduct, periodic value-chain assessment on human rights grounds, ethical procurement and sustainable sourcing, and ROHS certification for compliant procurement — relevant because the ATM, recycler, kiosk and surveillance-hardware business depends on third-party equipment.
- Risk and crisis management, including ESG and climate-related exposure — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk, on the rationale that effective risk and crisis management is vital for long-term financial planning and organisational flexibility, and that ESG and climate-related risks on the business and its stakeholders must be evaluated. The bundle's text on this row is truncated, so only the identification, not the full mitigation, is supported.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Strategy framed on four pillars: STRENGTHEN CORE ("Market share focus, large scale to drive lowest unit cost economics"; "World-class talent, tech & quality"), EXPAND TAM ("Forward & backward integration to offer customer value"), ROBUST PERFORMANCE ("High margin profile and FCF generation"; "Disciplined capital allocation") and PLATFORM APPROACH ("Each business to generate FCF to drive own growth").
- Through-cycle claim: "CMS across cycles: 11x revenue and 13x PAT since FY09", with milestone revenue markers of ₹216 Cr (FY09), ₹1,146 Cr (FY15, NPA Crisis & Demonetization), ₹1,129 Cr (FY19, COVID & Regulatory), ₹1,915 Cr (FY23, Post-IPO Competitive Intensity) and ₹2,487 Cr (FY26); the same slide states 15% Revenue CAGR and 16% PAT CAGR without naming the period.
- Customer mix is shifting: revenue mix moves from FY25 (SBI, Private Sector Banks/Retail, Managed Service Providers, PSU Banks shown as 24% / 26% / 34% / 16%) to FY26 (20% / 30% / 28% / 22%); the extract does not preserve which share binds to which customer group, so the pairing is not asserted here.
- Contract franchise: "Large multi-year contracts now signed with three of India's largest banks in 18 months"; board and management bench includes Rajiv Kaul (Exec. VC, WTD & CEO, 30+ years), plus directors Shyamala Gopinath (Former Deputy Governor, RBI) and Sunil Mehta (Former MD & CEO - PNB, CEO Indian Banks' Association).

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: CMS provides outsourced logistics and technology services to banks, financial institutions, organised retail and e-commerce companies in India. On any given day it manages cash replenishment and reconciliation across 70,000+ ATMs, services over 65,000 retail touchpoints, runs approximately 1,400 currency-in-transit routes across 20,000 bank branches, monitors over 50,000 sites through its HAWKAI Vision AI platform and powers ATM software on 65,000 machines through ALGO MVS. The business is organised into three platforms — ATM Management Solutions, Retail Solutions and Currency Logistics, and Technology and Payment Solutions — with the company processing approximately Rs 14 lakh Cr through its network annually.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **ATM Management Solutions:** ATM cash logistics, Brown Label ATM (BLA) management, Pure managed services, ATM ancillary services, Banking automation — supply, installation and maintenance of ATMs, currency recyclers and self-service kiosks, Branch transformation solutions
- **Retail Solutions and Currency Logistics:** Retail cash management, Currency-in-transit, Bullion logistics, Retail 360 Solution, Retail Cash Vault (RCV) machines, Cash processing and reconciliation at vaults and processing centres
- **Technology and Payment Solutions:** HAWKAI — Vision AI / AIoT remote monitoring platform, CMS Edge Chipset Device and HAWKAI Surveillance Camera, ALGO MVS — ATM multi-vendor software platform, Payment cards — card personalization and end-to-end financial card issuance and management

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Transform from a pure-play cash logistics provider into a broad-based business services platform, built over more than a decade by investing ahead of the curve, building rather than buying capability where possible, and entering new markets only with a differentiated offering.
- Compete only for fixed-price service contracts and stop bidding for contracts linked to transaction volumes — accepting lower short-term revenue for better quality and certainty of future earnings — while expanding wallet share in private banks.
- Deploy the large contracts won in FY25 and early FY26 as the top priority, with ICICI Bank and India Post Payments Bank approximately 90% operational at year end and full revenue starting in FY27.
- Improve efficiency through ML-driven route optimisation, which lifted capacity efficiency by 10% between September 2025 and March 2026, and cut 10%+ of routes.
- Shift retail delivery to a flexible gig workforce model — around 2,500 gig partners covering over 20% of retail locations — converting fixed wages into variable costs and making semi-urban and rural expansion viable.
- Grow Technology and Payment Solutions as the fastest-growing pillar (7% of services revenue in FY22 to 16% in FY26), owning the full Vision AI stack and extending HAWKAI beyond BFSI into quick commerce, EV charging, QSR and organised retail.
- Use disciplined M&A to consolidate the market — Securens for Vision AI leadership and the FSS Managed Services acquisition to consolidate MSP share and add direct banking client relationships.
- Rationalise low-yield retail points and dedicated vans, trading FY26 revenue for yield and margin quality.
- Position as the integrated, well-funded consolidator as weaker cash-logistics players exit, competing on technology capability, service quality and financial stability rather than lowest price.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: CMS is an asset-light services business, so its expansion is network, platform and contract build-out rather than plant capacity. FY26 was a step-up year: consolidated tangible and intangible asset addition was Rs 3,520 million, reflecting build-out for major new contracts, and came after two years of subdued capex averaging less than Rs 1,000 million; the Board's Report separately states that total tangible and intangible assets addition by the Company during FY26 was Rs 3,399.38 million. Management describes the capex profile as shifting: where post-listing capex went largely into cash logistics infrastructure and the Brown Label ATM business, FY26's Rs 352 Cr spend was predominantly HAWKAI and managed services, now on fixed-price contracts. The build-out is contract-led — network capacity was created ahead of a large public sector bank contract that was delayed, and the ICICI Bank and India Post Payments Bank deployments were approximately 90%+ live at year end with full ramp expected by Q1 FY27; entering FY27 the ATM pipeline covers RFP processes for 6,000-8,000 ATM units. Expansion also came through M&A: Securens Systems Private Limited was acquired (stated at Rs 70 Cr in the MD&A and Rs 75 Cr in the Chairman's message), taking CMS to 36% share and roughly double the scale of its nearest competitor in Vision AI, and a binding agreement for the FSS Managed Services acquisition (Rs 115 Cr) is signed with closure expected in H1 FY27. Efficiency rather than physical addition carries much of the growth: ML-driven route optimisation improved capacity efficiency by 10% between September 2025 and March 2026, and around 2,500 gig partners now cover over 20% of retail locations, making semi-urban and rural expansion viable without proportional fixed assets. Since IPO the Company reports cumulative capex investments of ~Rs 1,000 Cr and accretive acquisitions of ~Rs 190 Cr, all funded from operating cash flow, with a stated minimum 20% post-tax IRR hurdle for M&A and a stated hunt for small and mid-sized businesses in banking software and payments infrastructure, Vision AI applications in new sectors and specialised logistics. Note on quantum: the two NAMED DISCLOSURE blocks supplied in this bundle (capital commitments and segment capital expenditure) arrive flagged as ambiguous with no unit printed and no attributable period, so no rupee capex figure from them is usable and capex_disclosed is correctly empty.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Continued outsourcing of ATM operations, particularly by large public sector banks, where over 100,000 ATMs are yet to be outsourced.
- Banks replacing traditional ATMs with cash recyclers and automating branches, broadening the outsourcing opportunity beyond hardware into technology, software and end-to-end managed services — described as a Rs 10,000 Cr TAM.
- The ATM interchange fee hike from Rs 17 to Rs 19 per cash withdrawal effective May 2025, improving unit economics for banks and making outsourcing more attractive; India's interchange remains a fraction of US and European levels.
- Industry consolidation: weaker players have exited or faced operational difficulties, and in FY25 the #3 MSP ceased operations, moving the industry toward fewer, larger, better-capitalised players.
- Structurally low ATM density — 25 ATMs per 100,000 adults in India against a global average of 40 — with currency in circulation having doubled in eight years.
- India's formalisation of retail trade, expansion of organised retail into smaller cities and towns, quick commerce growth, NBFC branch expansion and bank branch network growth driven by financial inclusion.
- BFSI automation demand and under-penetration of remote monitoring: only approximately 40% of India's estimated 375,000 banking touchpoints currently use remote monitoring solutions.
- Vision AI addressable market exceeding Rs 8,000 Cr annually — approximately Rs 3,000 Cr in BFSI and Rs 5,000 Cr across non-BFSI verticals still largely on passive CCTV.
- Cash and digital payments treated as complementary rather than substitutive, with monthly currency dispensed through India's ATM network remaining robust and semi-urban/rural per-transaction withdrawals leading.
- Macro backdrop for FY27: real GDP growth of 6.5-7.0%, inflation of 3.5-4.0% and nominal GDP growth of approximately 10%.
- H2 FY26 recovery drivers carrying into FY27 — major contracts coming online, festive-season volume rebound, and the ICICI and SBI integrated contracts moving to full contribution.
- Margin levers: route optimisation, gig transition and automation pulling employee and service-security costs down as a percentage of revenue, which supported the Q4 recovery to a 25.6% EBITDA margin.
- CMS enters FY27 with a strong order book and clear visibility to revenue growth.
- Landmark win of the year: a Rs 1,000 Cr, 10-year integrated cash outsourcing mandate from State Bank of India covering 4,000 ATMs (cash logistics), the company's most significant public sector bank mandate to date.
- FY26 key wins: ICICI Bank fixed-price managed services with TCV of Rs 400 Cr+, SBI cash logistics over nine years with incremental TCV of Rs 500 Cr+, and HDFC Bank covering 6,000 ATMs over three years with TCV of Rs 400 Cr+.
- ICICI Bank and India Post Payments Bank contracts were approximately 90%+ live at year end, with full ramp expected by Q1 FY27.
- Entering FY27 the ATM pipeline is described as very strong with a clear preference towards recyclers: RFP processes for 6,000-8,000 ATM units representing a contracted-value opportunity of over Rs 20,000 million for the industry.
- Multi-year order book in ATM management from the SBI, ICICI Bank and India Post Payments Bank contracts.
